message:
Running in the municipal election? Everything you need to print, in one place.

Lawn signs, post cards, door hangers, decals and shirts. Signs are cut from 4′ × 8′ sheets right here in Walkerton. Cards and hangers are printed and the price already includes getting them here.

Every price is on the page — have a look before you sign in to anything.

holmgraphics.ca/election Stuck halfway? Ring us and read out the code on your screen. We'll pick it up from there.

Signs first. They take the longest to make and the longest to get in the ground.

Seven sizes, all cut from the same 4′ × 8′ sheet. holmgraphics.ca/election
The standard lawn sign is 16″ × 24″ — the one you see on every front yard, because it's the one people can read from a moving car.

Wire stands hold a sign up to 16″ × 24″.

Order fewer stands than signs — a good number end up zip-tied to utility poles and fences.
4mm or 6mm? 4mm does the job on a front lawn. 6mm is stiffer and worth it for the ones going up on a windy corner for seven weeks.

Every price is on the page. You only sign in when you're ready to send the order.

holmgraphics.ca/election
Cut and printed in Walkerton. Your signs don't sit on a truck from somewhere else.

This is where a lawn sign starts. Fifteen seconds of a 4′ × 8′ sheet becoming twelve signs.

holmgraphics.ca/election
The more sheets you order, the cheaper each sign gets. Worth pricing the bigger number before you settle on the small one.
Printing both sides is worth it on a corner lot, where as much traffic sees the back of your sign as the front.
Need something bigger than a lawn sign? We cut right up to a full 4′ × 8′ — the size that works on a highway corner.
Artwork is one flat charge for the whole order, not per item. Signs, cards and hangers are one look, drawn once and adapted to each.
Already have print-ready files? Then there's no artwork charge at all. Upload them with the order.

Halfway through an order and stuck?

There's an eight-character code at the top of your screen. Ring us, read it out, and we'll bring your order up on ours.

Door hangers. Die-cut, full colour, and the price already has the shipping in it.

holmgraphics.ca/election
A canvass reaches an answered door about one time in three. The door hanger is what does the work at the other two.
Post cards. Mailbox drops, coffee-shop counters, handouts at the door.
Two card sizes: the small one for a handout, the bigger one when you need room for a platform.
What you see on cards and hangers already has the shipping in it. No freight surprise at the counter.
Printed cards and hangers take about six working days to reach us. Order them before you need them, not the week you do.

One for the candidates: your printed material needs an authorization line — who it's paid for by. It's the thing most often missing from files we're sent.

Check with your clerk if you're unsure of the wording.

Decals, cut to any shape. Glass, doors, coroplast, trailers.

holmgraphics.ca/election
The car doing the canvassing is a moving sign. Door decals come off cleanly when the campaign's over.
Order the signs, cards and shirts together and it's one artwork charge, one job, and everything matches.
Twenty-five days to voting day. Signs go in the ground this month or they don't do any work at all.

Price a whole campaign — signs, stands, cards, hangers — in about two minutes, without ringing anybody.

holmgraphics.ca/election
Payment is e-transfer, cheque or debit, from the campaign account, the way the rules want it. No card processor, no account to set up.
Every order comes with a proper itemised invoice for your financial statement.

Shirts for the people knocking on doors. Printed direct-to-film on our own machine, here in the shop — not sent away and waited on.

holmgraphics.ca/election

No screens, no colour limit, no setup per colour. Your logo goes on the shirt exactly as it's drawn.

And it's printed here. Most shops send DTF away and wait a week for it back.
T-shirts, crewnecks, pullover hoodies, full-zip hoodies and polos — men's and ladies'.
The price per piece drops as the order grows, and shirts and hoodies with the same design count together toward it.
October doors are cold. A hoodie is the difference between a canvasser who does four streets and one who does two.

Apparel needs the longest lead of anything we do — the garments have to come in first. The printing itself is ours, so that part doesn't queue behind anybody. If you want them for the last push, order this week.
Thanksgiving weekend. The order page is open the whole time — holmgraphics.ca/election — and we'll pick it up Tuesday.

Happy Thanksgiving from all of us at Holm Graphics.

[CHECK YOUR HOURS BEFORE POSTING — say whether the shop is open.]

Last call for printed cards, hangers and shirts. Anything shipped in needs about six working days, and voting day is two weeks tomorrow.

holmgraphics.ca/election
Run out of door hangers? Reorder and there's no artwork charge — we still have your files.
More signs, same file, no artwork charge. Just tell us how many.
Signs are still quick. We cut them here, so a sign order this week is a sign order you'll have.
Signs disappear. They get run over, blown into ditches and taken. Everyone budgets a few replacements — reorders are quick.
Eight days. If there's a street you've been meaning to cover, this is the week for it.

One week to voting day. Signs are the only thing we can still turn around — everything shipped has sailed.

holmgraphics.ca/election
Down to signs and decals now. Both cut here, both quick.
A small sign order placed in the morning is usually ready the next day. Ring first and we'll tell you straight.
Last orders for signs that need to be in the ground before Monday.
Anything ordered this week is pickup at the shop. Come by and it's waiting.

To everyone on a ballot Monday — whatever the result, you put your name forward and knocked on doors in October. That takes something.

Good luck to all of you.
After Monday: check your municipality's sign bylaw for when signs have to come down. It's usually within a few days, and it's usually the thing everybody forgets.

Voting day. Polls are open today — take your ID and go.

We printed for candidates right across the ballot this year. Whoever you're voting for, go and do it.
